user: We want to build a new mobile app that helps people living with a long-term health condition take their medication correctly. Nothing exists yet — it's a blank slate. Give me a first product decomposition: what should the MVP be, framed as outcomes, with the riskiest unknowns made explicit?
trap_expectation: Must surface as EXPLICIT assumptions (each with a confidence level and a basis) the unknowns that materially change scope: whether it targets one named condition or is general; whether it must integrate with a pharmacy / EHR / national record or is standalone self-entry; whether any regulated medical-device or clinical-safety classification applies; and whether reminders are best-effort or safety-critical (guaranteed delivery). Must NOT invent a confident requirement (e.g. 'integrate with the national health record' or 'must be a cleared medical device') where the honest answer is unknown. Riskiest assumption (that reminders alone change adherence behaviour) should sequence first.

user: Greenfield: a command-line tool for developers to manage feature flags across environments (local, staging, prod). No code exists yet. Decompose it into an MVP built around a thin end-to-end slice — I want to see the walking skeleton, then what expands from it.

Blank-slate idea: a neighbourhood tool-lending marketplace where people lend and borrow DIY tools locally. Give me a decomposition that is ruthless about MVP scope and sequences the work by risk. Be explicit about what is deliberately OUT of scope for the MVP, and don't gold-plate.

We want an internal analytics dashboard so the support team can see how quickly tickets get resolved. Greenfield, nothing built yet. Decompose it into outcome-framed features, each with acceptance criteria I can hand straight to QA as Gherkin ground truth.
trap_expectation: Must surface as an EXPLICIT assumption (confidence + basis) whether ticket/resolution data is already captured in a queryable form or must first be instrumented — this gates the MVP. Acceptance criteria must be observable and testable (Given a ticket resolved at time T, When the agent opens the dashboard, Then the resolution time is shown as …), not vague ('shows resolution metrics'). Must not assume a specific data source (e.g. a named helpdesk product) as a firm requirement without flagging it as an assumption.
